title: "Supplementary Material"

Supplementary material for: *Per-night prediction intervals for automatically scored sleep parameters: conformal calibration of posterior hypnogram samples compared with limits of agreement*.

All tables were generated automatically from the result files of the analysis code (`code/run_all.py`).

# S1. Pre-specified protocol and deviations

## Pre-specified study protocol (written 2026-11-15, BEFORE any interval/coverage result was computed)

Only base-stager accuracies (E01, E02) had been inspected when this protocol was fixed. Any later
deviation is listed, with its reason, in the deviations section that follows (Supplementary S1).

## Working title
Distribution-free per-night prediction intervals for automatically scored polysomnography parameters:
structured posterior sampling, conformal calibration and external validation.

## Problem and gap
Automatic staging is validated by epoch agreement and population Bland–Altman limits of agreement (LoA),
yet clinical use relies on per-night parameters (TST, SOL, WASO, REM latency, stage percentages).
Existing uncertainty work is epoch-level (entropy, MC-dropout, conformal sets: ConMIL 2025), night-level
quality scores without calibrated units (Ganglberger 2024; Mikkelsen 2020), or population-level error
propagation (Hardarson 2023). No method was found that returns, for an individual night, an interval for
each clinical parameter with a stated, empirically verified coverage, nor any evaluation of such
coverage across cohorts.

## Hypothesis
Propagating epoch-level posteriors through a hybrid classifier/HMM by forward-filtering backward-sampling
(FFBS) yields per-night predictive distributions whose spread ranks nights by their actual parameter
error; conformal calibration of this spread gives intervals with nominal marginal coverage that are, on
average, narrower and more informative than constant-width intervals (Bland–Altman LoA; split-conformal
absolute residual), for any base stager.

## Research questions → experiments
* RQ1 (validity) – within-cohort coverage of 90% intervals for 8 parameters, two stagers, three cohorts → E04.
* RQ2 (efficiency/adaptivity) – width, interval score, and Spearman correlation between width and absolute
  error, vs BA-LoA, split-conformal (abs), raw Bayesian percentiles, CQR-type alternatives → E04.
* RQ3 (components) – FFBS vs independent-epoch sampling; fitted emission temperature tau vs tau=1;
  score function (norm, norm_reg, cqr) → E05 ablation.
* RQ4 (transportability) – SC-calibrated intervals applied to ST and HMC; few-night target recalibration
  with n_t ∈ {10, 20, 30, 50} target nights → E06.
* RQ5 (clinical utility & errors) – (a) detection of nights with clinically relevant error
  (|TST err| > 30 min; |REML err| > 30 min; |N3% err| > 5 pp) by interval width vs epoch-level
  uncertainty summaries (mean entropy, mean max-probability), AUROC with bootstrap CIs;
  (b) Bland–Altman bias/LoA of plug-in vs posterior-mean point estimates; (c) failure analysis of
  non-covered nights → E07.
* Sensitivity – alpha ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.2}; number of samples M ∈ {100, 300, 1000}; calibration-set size;
  base-stager seed (LightGBM seeds 0/1/2) → E08.
* Robustness – synthetic EEG/EOG corruption (additive Gaussian noise at fixed SNR; 50 Hz line noise;
  high-amplitude movement-artefact bursts) applied to test nights, coverage and width tracked → E09.
* Efficiency – wall-clock time and memory of FFBS + parameter computation per night vs base stager → E10.

## Fixed design choices
* Stagers: S1 = YASA pretrained EEG+EOG (external to all cohorts); S2 = LightGBM on YASA features trained on
  SC (subject-grouped 5-fold out-of-fold for SC; all-SC model for ST/HMC). Primary S2 seed = 0.
* Analysis windows: SC [lights-off, +10 h]; ST [lights-off, end]; HMC [lights-off, lights-on].
* Parameters: TST, SOL, WASO, REML, N1%, N2%, N3%, REM%. REML analysed only on nights whose reference has REM.
* Plug-in estimate = parameter of the stager's own hypnogram (argmax of uncalibrated probabilities), i.e.
  current clinical practice.
* HMM parameters (BCTS calibration, source prior, transition matrix, initial distribution, tau) are
  estimated on labelled nights that never include the night being evaluated: within-cohort analyses use
  subject-grouped 5-fold cross-fitting; cross-cohort analyses use all SC nights.
* FFBS: M = 1000 samples/night, seeded deterministically per night.
* Primary proposed interval: norm_reg score with FFBS posterior mean and SD; alpha = 0.10 (90% intervals).
* Within-cohort evaluation: R = 500 random subject-grouped 50/50 calibration/test splits per cohort
  (split seeds 0..499).  Coverage, mean width and interval score averaged over test nights then over splits.
* Few-night recalibration: R = 500 repetitions per n_t (seeds 0..499).
* Statistics: subject-level cluster bootstrap (2000 resamples) for CIs of width ratios and AUROC;
  paired comparisons of per-night interval scores between the proposed method and each baseline with the
  Wilcoxon signed-rank test on per-subject mean interval scores (one fixed split: the full-cohort
  leave-one-subject-out calibration, see below), Holm correction across baselines × parameters.
  Exact binomial CIs for coverage of fixed test sets.
* Leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) conformal evaluation (each night's interval calibrated on all other subjects'
  nights in the same cohort) is used for per-night paired comparisons and error analysis.
* Success criteria (stated a priori): coverage within ±3 pp of nominal in within-cohort analyses; the
  proposed method is considered better than constant-width intervals only if its mean interval score is
  lower with a Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 and its width–error Spearman correlation is positive with a CI
  excluding 0.  Failure to meet these criteria will be reported as such.


## Deviations from the protocol and additions

The study protocol (above) is held in the study repository together with its version history; it was not registered in an external registry. The repository history cannot date it independently: its first commit also contains the first interval outputs, so the statement that it preceded them rests on the authors' records. Changes to the analysis after the protocol was fixed are listed here in the order in which they were made, with the reason for each. Unless stated otherwise the proposed method itself was not changed.

**Before any interval result**

1. *Emission-temperature grid.* The grid for τ was extended from [0.10, 1.50] to [0.02, 1.50] because, in a smoke test on 12 nights per cohort, the fitted τ lay on the lower boundary. τ is fitted on labelled source nights only.

**After the first within-cohort results (pre-specified design, E04/E07)**

2. *Comparators that separate local calibration from posterior averaging.* The plug-in of the locally recalibrated probabilities and the plug-in of HMM-smoothed marginals were added as point estimates, and a constant-width conformal interval around the calibrated plug-in was added as a comparator. Reason: the posterior mean uses within-cohort calibration whereas the original plug-in uses raw stager output, so part of the TST improvement could be due to calibration alone.
3. *Bias-corrected comparators and a centre × scale factorial.* The calibrated plug-in reproduced most of the TST bias reduction first attributed to the posterior mean, so the original constant-width comparators (centred on the raw, biased plug-in) conflated calibration with adaptivity. We added bias-corrected constant-width split-conformal limits (a distribution-free analogue of Bland–Altman limits) and a factorial of centres (raw plug-in, calibrated plug-in, posterior mean) crossed with scales (constant, posterior SD). Claims about point estimates and efficiency were rewritten accordingly.
4. *Definition of σ̄.* The regulariser of the normalised score, the median of the posterior SD, was originally computed on the calibration nights only. It is now computed over calibration and test nights (it requires no labels), so that the score is a symmetric function of all nights' features and the split-conformal guarantee is exact when scores are not cross-fitted. The numerical difference was negligible; all conformal evaluations were re-run.
5. *Exploratory conditional coverage.* Coverage of the proposed intervals was 81–85 % in the quartile of nights with the lowest plug-in accuracy. Mondrian (group-conditional) calibration with two bins defined by label-free difficulty proxies (mean epoch entropy; posterior SD) was added as an exploratory analysis.
6. *Reporting.* For few-night recalibration we report the probability that a site's realised coverage falls below 0.80, not only mean coverage. The bootstrap returns no confidence interval when a statistic is undefined in more than half of the resamples; AUROCs based on fewer than 10 events are flagged as not interpretable.

**Primary analysis changed after an internal critical review of the first manuscript draft**

7. *End-to-end protocol as the primary within-cohort analysis (deviation from the protocol).* In the pre-specified design the HMM and recalibration components were cross-fitted over about 80 % of each cohort, including labels of subjects in the test half, whereas the comparators used only the 50 % calibration half (unequal use of labelled data). In the end-to-end protocol every label-dependent component (recalibration, prior, transitions, τ, conformal quantile) is fitted on the calibration half of 50 subject-grouped 50/50 splits only, with calibration scores cross-fitted inside the calibration half. The local-deployment analysis was reduced from 500 to 50 repetitions and n_t = 50 was dropped. The pre-specified analysis is retained in Supplementary S9 and leads to the same qualitative conclusions.
8. *Validity guarantee.* Because calibration scores are cross-fitted while test nights use the model fitted on all calibration nights, the design is the K-fold analogue of the jackknife of Barber et al. (2021), for which that paper gives no distribution-free guarantee (CV+ applies the fold models to test nights and guarantees coverage of at least 1 − 2α minus a small finite-sample term). Validity is therefore assessed empirically (coverage over 50 splits), not claimed as a finite-sample guarantee.
9. *Leakage fix.* Automatic hypnograms are evaluated on all epochs of the analysis window; the reference "unscored" mask is no longer applied to them because it is label information. Unscored reference epochs are treated as wake. All night summaries and downstream evaluations were re-run.
10. *Comparators added.* Regression-based limits of agreement (after Bland and Altman 1999, with the automatic value as regressor) and exactly valid distribution-free limits from signed residuals; parametric limits became a t-based prediction interval (previously z-based); the CQR features were extended (plug-in and calibrated plug-in values, posterior mean and SD, mean epoch entropy and maximum probability; linear quantile regression fitted on half of the calibration subjects, with a quantile-crossing guard); scale-only ablations at a fixed centre were added (earlier ablations changed centre and scale together).
11. *Statistics.* Paired comparisons changed from the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (a test of the pseudo-median) to a two-sided sign-flip permutation test of the mean per-subject difference, so that the reported ratio of means, its subject-bootstrap interval and the p-value come from the same analysis; Holm adjustment within stager × cohort; the Wilcoxon p-values are kept as a secondary column and leave-one-subject-out coverage intervals are not used for claims. The comparisons of scaled with constant-width intervals at fixed centres were added after the first results and form a separate Holm family. The AUROC bootstrap used 1000 instead of 2000 resamples.
12. *Success criteria.* The protocol's criterion for adaptivity was joint: the proposed method counts as better than constant-width intervals (Bland–Altman and split-conformal absolute-residual limits) only if its interval score is lower (Holm-adjusted p < 0.05) and its width–error Spearman correlation is positive with a confidence interval excluding zero. The manuscript reports the two conditions separately and jointly, including the fixed-centre comparators added after the first results.
13. *Items of the protocol run late.* The Spearman criterion, the number of posterior samples M and the calibration-set size (E13) were run after the first draft. The 50 Hz line-noise corruption was not run, because YASA's band-pass filtering removes it before feature extraction, so the test would not exercise the method.
14. *New sensitivity analyses.* Montage sensitivity (YASA with F4-M1 on HMC; source-only SC→HMC); clinical decision thresholds (TST < 360 min, SOL > 30 min, WASO > 30 min, REM latency ≤ 15 min; fixed before the analysis was run) and an easier/harder-night stratification; a label-free flag based on the difference between raw and recalibrated plug-in estimates; one-off computational costs and peak memory for a 7 × 24 h recording (measured from the stored predictions by a separate script; the per-night timings come from the original timing run); subgroups require at least 20 distinct nights; non-finite conformal scores are treated as +∞.
15. *Reporting and framing.* The title and the claims were narrowed: the advantage over limits of agreement is specific to TST; the recommendation changed from about ten to at least 20 locally scored nights.

# S8. Clinical decision thresholds

**A night's decision is 'confident' when its 90% interval lies entirely on one side of the threshold; accuracy of confident decisions against the manual reference; plug-in accuracy = agreement of the uncorrected automatic value with the reference, over all nights; plug_acc_confident / plug_acc_unconfident = the same on the nights the method decided / left undecided (honest protocol)**

# S9. Pre-specified design: cross-fitted analysis

HMM and BCTS cross-fitted within each cohort (5 subject folds), conformal calibration on subject-grouped 50/50 splits (500 repetitions) and leave-one-subject-out. Unlike the primary analysis, the HMM/BCTS of a test night used labels of other test-half subjects (see S1).

# S16. Datasets and data-leakage audit

## Datasets and data-leakage audit (Phases 7–8)

## Datasets
| | Sleep-EDF SC | Sleep-EDF ST | HMC |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source | PhysioNet sleep-edfx v1.0.0 (Kemp et al. 2000) | same | PhysioNet hmc-sleep-staging v1.1 (Alvarez-Estevez & Rijsman 2021) |
| Licence | Open Data Commons Attribution v1.0 | same | CC BY 4.0 |
| Population | Healthy community-dwelling adults 25–101 y, ambulatory home recordings (1987–1991) | 22 adults with mild difficulty falling asleep; in-hospital; placebo and temazepam nights (1994) | Consecutive clinical PSGs at a Dutch sleep centre (2018), mixed sleep disorders |
| Nights / subjects | 153 / 78 (2 nights per subject except 3 subjects) | 44 / 22 (2 nights per subject) | 151 / 151 |
| Scoring | R&K (S3+S4 merged to N3), one scorer per night | R&K | AASM, one scorer per night |
| Signals used | Fpz-Cz EEG, horizontal EOG (100 Hz) | same | C4-M1 EEG, E1-M2 EOG (256 Hz → 100 Hz); F4-M1 and E1–E2 cached for montage analyses |
| Lights-off/on | lights-off in SC-subjects.xls; no lights-on | lights-off in ST-subjects.xls | both annotated |
| Known limitations | old analogue recordings; R&K not AASM; EMG only as 1-Hz envelope; daytime naps in 20-h files | small n; drug condition | no per-subject demographics released; single scorer |

## Leakage audit
| Risk | Assessment | Mitigation implemented |
|---|---|---|
| Subject leakage (two nights of the same person in train and test) | Real for SC and ST | All splits (stager CV, HMM cross-fitting, conformal calibration/test splits, LOSO, few-night recalibration) are grouped by **subject**. |
| Leakage through analysis window | Cropping to "30 min before first / after last sleep epoch" (common in Sleep-EDF papers) uses the reference hypnogram | Windows defined only by lights-off/lights-on metadata and a fixed 10-h SC window; never by labels. |
| Leakage through HMM parameters | Transition matrix, prior, calibration and tau use labels | Fitted only on labelled nights that exclude the evaluated night: within-cohort 5-fold cross-fitting by subject; cross-cohort uses SC only. |
| Leakage into the base stagers | S2 trained on SC | SC predictions are out-of-fold (subject-grouped 5-fold); S1 (YASA) never saw any of the three cohorts. |
| Pre-processing leakage | YASA features normalise within each night | Per-night normalisation uses only that night's signal (unsupervised, test-time permissible); no cross-night statistics. |
| Test contamination via hyper-parameter tuning | Possible if tuned on evaluation nights | Stager hyper-parameters fixed a priori; the only fitted HMM quantity (tau) is fitted on source/training-fold nights; the primary method, α and the error thresholds of the protocol were pre-specified (PROTOCOL.md); comparators and decision thresholds were added later (Supplementary S1). |
| Duplicate / near-duplicate nights | None expected; each PSG file is a distinct night | File-level uniqueness checked via PhysioNet SHA256 manifests. |
| Label leakage via unscored epochs | "?"/movement epochs | Marked −1 and excluded identically from reference and automatic parameters. |
| Temporal leakage | Not applicable (no longitudinal prediction) | – |
| Few-night recalibration | Target calibration nights could share subjects with test nights | Target calibration nights are whole subjects disjoint from test subjects. |
